thread.title: Spotify is in talks to buy podcast network Gimlet Media for $230 million (SPOT, AAPL, NFLX, MSFT, F)

author: Audrey Schomer
title: Spotify is in talks to buy podcast network Gimlet Media for $230 million (SPOT, AAPL, NFLX, MSFT, F)

organizations.name: business insider intelligence venture-backed startup gimlet

text: Audrey Schomer 2m This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence " Digital Media Briefing " subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here . Spotify is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Brooklyn-based podcast network Gimlet Media for $230 million , per Recode. Business Insider Intelligence Venture-backed startup Gimlet has raised about $28.5 million in funding to date, from investors like WPP and Emerson Collective. The acquisition would mark the biggest in the relatively young podcast industry, and the first time that Spotify will have purchased a content producer. Spotify reports Q4 earnings on Wednesday — we'll likely hear more about its plans then. The potential acquisition signals a growing push by the music streaming giant to partially liberate itself from licensing fees. Spotify made some moves in 2018 that suggest a growing desire to bypass music labels, for example, by launching a direct-upload tool for indie artists last September. Owning content that it distributes on the platform frees Spotify of additional licensing commitments, which are significant, and a main reason why the company continues to operate at a loss. Spotify has paid out some $10 billion to labels since 2006, and typically pays labels about 52% of the revenue generated by each stream of a song. As Spotify grows as a destination for podcast fans — in January it reported that podcast listening on the platform had surged 175% year-over-year (YoY) — owning the content becomes even more valuable. Bolstering its podcast offerings would also help Spotify expand its overall content product and — importantly — its ad opportunities. Podcasts aren't entirely new to the platform, but the acquisition would strengthen its offerings in two ways: Diversified content. Spotify's podcast strategy has so far involved tapping celebrities like Amy Schumer and Jemele Hill to make platform-exclusive pods. Having a content production company under its roof would instantly give Spotify a wide range of successful audio content assets, as well as the capability to become a producer at greater scale, similar to how Netflix has transformed itself into a studio over time. Gimlet Media produces a network of hit podcasts, including "Homecoming," which has been turned into an Amazon original series. Branded content. Under its in-house agency Gimlet Creative, Gimlet produces branded narrative audio shows for companies like Ford, Microsoft, Audible, Sonos, Squarespace, and Spotify. Spotify could further leverage Gimlet's branded content capabilities as an additional growth engine for still relatively lagging ad revenue at the company, particularly if it can drive users to engage with branded audio on the service. Spotify's large global audience could help it overcome typical concerns around podcast monetization, allowing it to attain a more formidable position in the still-forming landscape. Podcasting generated just $315 million in ad revenue in 2017, per IAB. While spend on the medium is relatively low, it's fast-growing, up 86% YoY, per IAB. Still, podcast monetization remains difficult: Podcasters typically aren't eligible to advertise in their shows without first getting about 20,000 downloads, and the average number of downloads is just 1,600, per the Business Insider Intelligence Podcast Report. But Spotify has 200 million MAU worldwide. If the platform can scale podcasts across its global user base, it will be more likely to attract willing content partners and publishers seeking a surer bet. And, eventually, it could start taking incremental share of consumption and listenership from dedicated podcast hosting apps like Apple Podcasts, Google Play Music, and Stitcher.
